- `python` and `pip` run only inside the Appendix A container (fixflow-pr-reviewer.md:33; there is no python on PATH).

3) The "copy untracked files" half has nothing to carry here and would work against the plan. The main checkout holds only backend/.env.example, with no backend/.env and no .venv. SHIP-PLAN P1 (:359-360) requires a test run in a cleaned environment "with no inherited backend/.env or compose env". The silent-skip case NEW-A cites (a missing DB URL skipping integration tests) is exactly what P1's skip-aware gate catches (SHIP-PLAN :361-363; HARNESS-REVIEW :263).

4) The "generic create-worktree script plus automatic cleanup" half does not fit this setup. The Claude desktop app creates the .claude/worktrees/* worktrees, so a repo script that also creates them would compete with the app. Cleanup on failure deletes directories, which is the kind of destructive step the harness keeps behind an owner decision.

5) The only gap left is dependencies for the native web and mobile gates. Of the four worktrees, three have no root node_modules and none has technician-app/node_modules. But that failure is loud (vitest or jest not found), not silent, and the fix is npm ci in two directories. No session has recorded lost time from it. The Windows long-path memory is about git clones into the scratchpad, not worktree setup. W3 also applies: the routine has never run, so there is no observed cost to fix.
refutation.what_would_settle_it: Fold this into G2-F168's record; do not keep a second family. That is a line in the skill, not a script: no file copying, no .worktreeinclude for .env, no cleanup. If (c) occurs, that is a compliance problem with an existing rule (W2), not a reason to build a setup script.
